result.summary: The street environment provides a sidewalk and tree buffer on the residential side, but the opposite side lacks a continuous walkway, forcing pedestrians into a parking lot or the roadway. The presence of a bike lane and bus stop markings indicates multi-modal use, yet the absence of marked crossings and the wide road geometry prioritize vehicle speed.

hazards.name: Missing sidewalk on left side
hazards.description: Pedestrians on the left side of the image have no dedicated walkway and must navigate through a parking lot or walk in the bike lane.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible crosswalks for a significant distance, requiring pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic unprotected.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a safe path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with high-visibility paint and signage to designate a safe crossing point.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Build out the curb at potential crossing points to reduce the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility to drivers.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection that lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals. A large recreational vehicle parked near the corner creates a significant visual obstruction, further compromising safety at this crossing.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked RV
hazards.description: A large recreational vehicle parked close to the intersection severely limits sightlines between pedestrians and approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalks
hazards.description: The absence of painted crosswalks at a signalized intersection fails to designate a safe path for pedestrians or alert drivers to their presence.

hazards.name: Absence of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signals are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals which may not provide adequate crossing time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks on all legs of the intersection to improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the intersection to restore sightlines, potentially using curb extensions or bollards.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Heads
interventions.description: Install pedestrian countdown signals to provide clear information on when it is safe to cross and how much time remains.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban arterial road with multiple travel lanes and a painted median. While sidewalks and marked crosswalks are present, the environment is dominated by vehicle traffic with long crossing distances and no physical buffers for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic and a wide painted median, increasing exposure time to vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of sidewalk buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right is directly adjacent to a travel lane with no physical barrier or planting strip to protect pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised concrete island in the median at the intersection to allow pedestrians to cross in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the intersection corners to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the roadway to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide but severely degraded paved area that lacks clear separation from the roadway. The presence of a bus stop marking without designated crossing infrastructure or a sidewalk buffer creates a high-risk environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The paved walkway is heavily cracked and uneven, creating significant trip hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and mid-ground paved area in front of the red building.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or buffer between the pedestrian area and the active bus lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Edge of the roadway adjacent to the 'BUS' marking.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstructions
hazards.description: Multiple utility poles are located within the walking path, narrowing the effective clear width.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, within the paved walkway.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Repave the walkway to provide a smooth, continuous, and ADA-compliant surface.

interventions.title: Streetscape Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or furniture zone with trees or bollards to separate pedestrians from the roadway.

interventions.title: Bus Stop Enhancements
interventions.description: Add a bus shelter and a marked midblock crosswalk with appropriate signage to improve safety for transit users.
